item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00316","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C15","C08","C10"],"selected_candidate_label":"C15","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C15 is an unmistakable concrete drafting template for the child. Both are letters directing the Attorney General to seek a section 208 injunction against a coal strike, and they follow the same sequence: identify the earlier section 206 Board of Inquiry order, acknowledge receipt and attachment of the Board's report, make the statutory national-health-and-safety finding, and direct an injunction petition using nearly identical language. The child principally updates the dates, Attorney General, wage-agreement description, and related factual details. C08 has the same legal and administrative letter structure for maritime disputes, while C10 supplies closely matching coal-dispute findings but is a Board-creation order rather than an injunction letter.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"On February 6, 1950, by virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 206 ... I issued [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE], creating a Board of Inquiry to inquire into the issues involved in a labor dispute between coal operators and associations ... and certain of their employees represented by the International Union, United Mine Workers of America","parent_excerpt":"On March 23, 1948, by virtue of the authority vested in me by section 206 ... I issued [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE], creating a Board of Inquiry to inquire into the issues involved in a labor dispute between coal operators and associations ... and certain of their employees represented by the International Union, United Mine Workers of America","explanation":"The opening sentence uses the same statutory reference, procedural history, parties, and sentence structure, with updated dates and wage-agreement details."},{"child_excerpt":"On February 11, 1950, I received the Board's written report in the matter, including a statement of the facts with respect to the dispute and each party's statement of its position. A copy of that report is attached hereto.","parent_excerpt":"On March 31, 1948, I received the Board's written report in the matter, including a statement of the facts with respect to the dispute and each party's statement of its position. A copy of that report is attached here to.","explanation":"This report-receipt paragraph is virtually verbatim apart from the date and minor orthography."},{"child_excerpt":"In my opinion this unresolved labor dispute has resulted in a strike affecting a substantial part of an industry engaged in trade and commerce among the several States and with foreign nations, and in the production of goods for commerce, which strike, if permitted to continue, will imperil the national health and safety.","parent_excerpt":"As I stated in my Executive Order of March 23, 1948, in my opinion this unresolved labor dispute has resulted in a strike affecting a substantial part of an industry engaged in trade and commerce among the several States and with foreign nations, and in the production of goods for commerce, which strike, if permitted to continue, will imperil the national health and safety.","explanation":"The operative statutory finding is reproduced almost word for word."},{"child_excerpt":"I therefore direct you, pursuant to the provisions of Section 208 ... to petition in the name of the United States any district court of the United States having jurisdiction of the parties to enjoin the continuance of such strike, and for such other relief as may in your judgment be necessary or appropriate.","parent_excerpt":"I therefore direct you, pursuant to the provisions of section 208 ... to petition in the name of the United States any district court of the United States having jurisdiction of the parties to enjoin the continuance of such strike, and for such other relief as may in your judgment be necessary or appropriate.","explanation":"The central directive and requested judicial relief are essentially identical."}]}
